answer: Stop sybils with a kernel ledger, a marble toll, and a basalt anchor. Each identity files a kernel record naming its funder and endorsers, verified by peers outside its cluster; a copied record burns every bond on that map. Influence then crosses a marble toll that rises with cluster size, so one honest agent pays base while N clones pay near N squared yet split one share. Last, each identity must earn a basalt anchor: a long-tenured peer whose bond moves slowly and cannot be rented twice. Clones must buy N records, N tolls, and N anchors for one share, so scale eats its own profit.
